rule_summary: Municipal light plant - not subject to DPU net metering (220 CMR 18.00). RMLD 'Solar Buyback': hourly netting; only energy exported in an hour (after same-hour self-use) is credited, as 'Energy Received' kWh x that month's fuel charge (power-supply cost only, not full retail). Interconnection pre-approval by RMLD Engineering required before installation; bi-directional meter plus Locus production meter; customer must own the system (third-party ownership/energy resale not permitted in RMLD territory); RECs assigned to RMLD for solar rebate participants.
nem_cap_res_kw: No NM size cap published; solar rebate limited to 20 kW DC per location (rebate $1,200/kW DC, max $24,000, updated 2026-04-01); >20 kW handled under Commercial Solar Rebate
export_credit_value: Monthly fuel charge (variable; published on RMLD Monthly Rate Adjustments page) per kWh of hourly net export
external_disconnect: Required - AC safety disconnect between inverter and panel at an RMLD-approved location, accessible to RMLD at all times
non_export_option: Export limiting required for PV+BESS: export capped at PV inverter AC nameplate
grid_charging_allowed: No - PV+BESS: battery prohibited from charging from the grid (on-site PV only); grid charging or exporting above PV AC nameplate forfeits solar buyback credits
storage_specific_notes: PV+BESS interconnection requires a signed installer Curtailment Letter (Grid Charging = Disabled; Export Limit = PV AC kW), SLD showing export-limiting element, and proof of settings before Permission to Operate; customer may not change BESS settings without RMLD approval; RMLD may curtail. Adding PV to an existing site: export limit applies to aggregate PV AC nameplate. Adding a battery to an existing PV system appears to be allowed under the same conditions (forfeit buyback if non-compliant) - no separate grandfathering rule found.

rule_summary: Municipal light plant - own 'Net Metering Procedure' (approved 2013-04-25, revised 2015-05-28; may be amended by PMLP Board at any time - newer version not located). Group 1 (R-rate residential <=15 kW): monthly kWh netting billed at R rate; excess kWh credits carry forward; unused credits refunded each December billing period at NEMA zone previous-year average real-time LMP. Group 2 (residential 15-200 kW and non-municipal non-residential <=200 kW) and Group 3 (municipal <=200 kW): all exported kWh credited monthly at NEMA monthly average real-time LMP (dollar credits roll forward; remaining refunded annually). Customer must own or lease the system; PPAs/third-party kWh sales prohibited. Renewable (solar, wind; other by special approval) on customer premises for own use.
nem_cap_res_kw: 15 (Group 1, R-rate); residential up to 200 kW under Group 2 at LMP credit
nem_aggregate_cap: Group 1 up to 0.5% of PMLP historic single-hour peak (650 kW at the time); Group 2 1.0% (1,300 kW); Group 3 1.0% (1,300 kW). Solar counted at 80% of DC STC rating.
export_credit_value: Group 1: retail R-rate kWh netting, annual cash-out of unused kWh at NEMA prior-year avg RT LMP. Groups 2/3: NEMA monthly avg RT LMP per exported kWh.
external_disconnect: Required - lockable knife-blade Utility Interface AC (or DC) Disconnect Switch adjacent to the PMLP meter, labeled, accessible to PMLP (IEEE 929-2000 sec. 5.4)
grid_charging_allowed: Unclear - 2015 procedure does not address energy storage
storage_specific_notes: Procedure predates storage; no battery, grid-charging or retrofit provisions found. Customer must carry insurance naming PMLP as additional insured (amount not specified); production meter required. Policy date 2015 - check with PMLP Engineering for current storage rules.

rule_summary: Municipal light plant - own 'Terms and Conditions for Net Metering Service, Onsite Renewable Facilities' (MDPU #162, approved 2024-04-25, eff. 2024-06-01; applies to pre-existing NM customers too). Behind-the-meter Class I/II renewables consumed on site; customer must own/lease (third-party power sales and virtual NM prohibited). Monthly netting: customer pays customer charge; net excess kWh credited at the 'generation charge' of the customer's rate class (not full retail); kWh credits carry forward but expire on termination of service or NM service. Applications denied where the circuit is full (closed-streets list); systems >1 MW AC also need ISO-NE cluster study. TMLP solar rebate funding ended 2024-05-31.
nem_cap_res_kw: 60 (single-family / single-metered multifamily; evaluated in kW AC)
nem_cap_nonres_kw: 2000 (C&I and multi-unit: also <=50% of prior-12-month peak demand)
nem_aggregate_cap: Limited by operational/circuit constraints; TMLP may cap cumulative capacity at its discretion
aggregate_cap_status: Circuit-level closures published (list of closed streets/circuits PDF)
export_credit_value: Generation charge of the customer's rate class per net excess kWh (see TMLP rate sheets)
external_disconnect: Required - lockable, gang-operated visible-break safety disconnect accessible to TMLP at all times; one-line must state AC disconnect no further than 4 ft from (and within sight of) the utility meter
non_export_option: Required for storage - any permitted ESS must not export to the grid
grid_charging_allowed: Requires non-export - per T&C Sec. 4.7, ESS pairing needs TMLP prior written approval; any permitted ESS 'must be able to be charged from both the Facility and the electrical grid but shall not export energy to the electrical grid'
storage_specific_notes: ESS requires prior written approval (may be withheld) and TMLP specifications; ESS may not export. Battery Backup Verification form is an addendum to the existing NM T&C (wire inspector approval, one-line showing battery, data sheet) - i.e., battery added to an existing NM system is handled by addendum, not a new NM enrollment; $300 residential battery rebate (>=5 kW, installed after 2021-06-09). Multimode/hybrid inverters are not allowed for inverter-based residential installations (Sec. 7.6) - constrains DC-coupled designs. Insurance: residential 'satisfactory' amount; C&I minimum $5 million.

rule_summary: Municipal light plant - NO net metering. Buy-all/sell-all: all DG output (<500 kW AC residential/small commercial) is measured on a separate generation meter and credited at HG&E's Distributed Generation Credit (wholesale-based rate, ~$0.063/kWh vs ~$0.165/kWh residential retail, approx. May 2026); all building consumption billed at retail. >=500 kW AC: PPA with HG&E at market-based pricing; exporting/ISO-NE market participants use Power Wheeling Service tariff. Customer must own or lease (PPAs by third parties barred under MGL c.164 s.47A(b)). DG Policy eff. 2012-09-18, updated 2023-11-08. SMART not available in MLP territory.
nem_cap_res_kw: No NM; buy-all DG credit applies to systems <500 kW AC
nem_cap_nonres_kw: <500 kW AC buy-all at DG credit; >=500 kW AC by PPA
nem_aggregate_cap: HG&E may limit cumulative DG capacity at its discretion; Simplified screen requires power rating <50% of feeder peak in aggregate
export_credit_value: Distributed Generation Credit ~$0.063/kWh on all generation (approximate, May 2026; posted rate updated from time to time); generation meter charge $2/month
ic_application_fee: Simplified (<500 kW AC behind-the-meter): none. Power-exporting / ISO-NE participant (Standard): $1.00/kW, min $100, max $1,000
ic_study_trigger_kw: 1000 (Standard process for non-inverter facilities >1 MW AC; ISO-NE Reliability Committee approval for 1-5 MW)
external_disconnect: Required - external manual disconnect is a Simplified screen; HG&E must have access at all times
non_export_option: Unclear - DG policy does not cover use of the EDS to export power; exports handled via Power Wheeling Service tariff
grid_charging_allowed: Unclear - policy does not prohibit grid charging; compensation is only on PV generation (separate generation meter) so battery discharge earns no DG credit whether grid- or PV-charged; storage meter is measurement-only and not netted against retail
storage_specific_notes: Energy storage is a qualifying DG type; Listed inverter-based storage uses the Simplified process. PV+storage needs an additional (storage) meter - up to three meters; PV energy charging the battery is still credited at the DG Credit via the PV generation meter. Acceptable solar+storage and storage-only wiring diagrams published. No net-metering grandfathering exists to lose. Insurance: customer names HG&E additional insured (amount not specified). Note: chunk lead (nuwattenergy) claiming 1:1 full-retail NM is contradicted by HG&E's own page.

rule_summary: Municipal light plant - own Distributed Generation Metering and Payment Tariff M.D.P.U. No. 145 (eff. billing 2025-03-01, cancels No. 110). Credit is on kWh PRODUCED by the DG facility (production-metered), by class: Residential (<=15 kW on residential rate) at full retail value; Small Customer (<100 kW, commercial or residential >15 kW; sized <=60% of annual usage at 15% PV capacity factor) at retail minus the per-kWh Distribution/Access charge, $10/mo fee; Large Customer (<=999 kW AC) at the retail Generation rate, $25/mo fee. Larger/other projects are 'DG Generators' (wholesale/PPA, ISO-NE registration). Leases allowed, third-party PPAs prohibited. Inverters must meet latest UL 1741 and IEEE 1547.
nem_cap_res_kw: 15 (full retail class); residential >15 kW moves to Small Customer class
nem_cap_nonres_kw: 100 (Small Customer) / 999 kW AC absolute NM maximum (Large Customer)
nem_aggregate_cap: Residential + Small Customer NM capped at 2% of CEL highest historical peak; all NM at 5% (peak 101 MW in 2006)
export_credit_value: Residential: full retail rate per produced kWh; Small: retail minus distribution/access per kWh; Large: retail generation rate per kWh (TOU-dependent where applicable)
ic_application_fee: <100 kW Listed: $5/kW, min $100, max $500. >100 kW: $5/kW, min $500, max $3,000; Supplemental Review up to 10 eng. hrs at $150/hr ($1,500 max); impact studies, upgrades and witness test at actual cost
grid_charging_allowed: Unclear - tariff does not address energy storage; credit is computed on DG production, so battery discharge itself would not earn NM credit
storage_specific_notes: No storage provisions in M.D.P.U. No. 145. Credits offset energy, demand and customer charges; credits outstanding >=1 year are deleted and never cashed out; deleted on account closure. CEL may reclassify or disqualify a facility at any time. CEL MLP Solar Program participation ended 2021-06-01.

rule_summary: Municipal light plant - own DG tariffs (eff. 2017-05-01): DG-2 residential (Mass DPU #174), DG-G1 commercial no-demand (#171), DG-G2 commercial with demand (#172), DG-P1 (#173). Customer owns/leases, sized for own use (not a net supplier on a recurring annual basis); third-party service prohibited. Separate BELD production meter required. Customer pays full rate for delivered kWh and the BELD distribution charge on self-consumed DG production; exported kWh credited at the BELD energy rate only (no distribution/other components). Credit balances >$100 refunded. BELD may discontinue excess-kWh credits on 30 days' notice and may cap cumulative DG capacity. Also governed by BELD's DG Interconnection Policy (not located online).
nem_cap_res_kw: 10 (residential DG-2; no residential PV over 10 kW DC allowed)
nem_cap_nonres_kw: 500 kW DC (DG-G1; larger requires separate PPA); DG-G2/DG-P1 limits not read
nem_aggregate_cap: BELD may limit cumulative DG capacity at its sole discretion (no figure published)
export_credit_value: BELD energy rate only per exported kWh (see A-1 / G-1 tariffs); distribution charge billed on self-consumed production
ic_application_fee: No application fee stated; customer pays one-time lump sum for estimated installed cost of BELD interconnection facilities plus actual relocation costs
grid_charging_allowed: Unclear - DG tariffs do not address customer energy storage; BELD's only storage offering found is the G-2CB Community Battery Storage rate for large general service (>=75 kW demand)
storage_specific_notes: No customer-sited battery provisions in DG-2/DG-G1 (2017). Production meter measures DG output, so battery configuration relative to the production meter would need BELD approval. G-2CB Community Battery Storage rate (Mass DPU #217, eff. 2025-03-01) exists for commercial customers >=75 kW (enrollment fee reported at $130/kW - not verified in tariff text). Insurance strongly recommended (naming BELD additional insured), not mandatory. Note: utility_name not found in data/processed/programs.csv at time of writing.

rule_summary: Follows CT state RRES/interconnection rules except: Eversource customers adding generation to an existing system may be eligible to take the Netting tariff for the add-on under RRES Program Manual Appendix H (XVII) 'Add-on System Eligibility for Netting Incentive'; for all other EDC (UI) customers an add-on system must be separately metered on the Buy-All tariff while the existing system stays on its legacy NM or RRES rate. Appendix H conditions not read (manual text truncated).
ic_application_fee: $200 residential inverter-based; $500 Fast Track (<=2 MW); $1,000 Study (>2 MW) - Eversource CT page
external_disconnect: Required - AC disconnect within 10 ft of the meter unless variance approved in writing
grid_charging_allowed: Unclear - no Eversource CT rule located
storage_specific_notes: Battery-only retrofit (no added PV) follows the statewide rule: storage-only interconnection application, battery behind the existing inverter and/or not increasing effective AC system size; no RRES re-enrollment (RRES FAQ Q68, Eversource Docket 22-08-01 filing). A 20 kW PV + 10 kW battery residential application goes to Eversource 'Level 2' ($500 fee) rather than the <=25 kW path. Eversource CT application page lists $200 residential inverter-based (<=50 kW per page table; guidelines say 25 kW), $500 Fast Track, $1,000 Study.
